transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12 14:00 UTC | Duration: 38m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Iris (Redwood CSM); Maya, David, Priya, Evan, Jordan, Tomas (Celerity)

Auto-summary (auto-gen):
- Week 3 of quant POC. INT8 increased throughput and reduced token cost ~2.8x vs FP16 for long-context gen. FP8 shows promise for steady-state quality on classification/NER tasks.
- Primary quality regressions concentrated on short-answer extraction & date parsing; hallucination uplift observed on 2 templates.
- Action: sensitivity sweep on 5k sample, run canary with KV-cache pinned, and produce canary rollback playbook.

Topics: pilot throughput deltas, quality drift signal analysis, KV cache and prefix-caching effects, fallback strategy, canary checklist, next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: okay everybody thanks for hopping on we are on week three of the quant pilot with Celerity, quick round of intros?
[00:08] Maya: Maya, ML eng. thanks.
[00:10] David: David, platform.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, SRE.
[00:14] Samir: Samir, Redwood SE. I'll run through the results and the sensitivity stuff.
[00:18] Evan: Evan, product.
[00:20] Jordan: Jordan QA.
[00:22] Tomas: Tomas research.
[00:24] Lena: great quick agenda: run through numbers, show the signal/heatmap we cooked up, discuss two failing templates, talk fallbacks and canary, wrap with next steps.

[02:00] Samir: all right numbers first. baseline is FP16 on your prod-like bench: median p99 token latency 120ms, throughput 140 tokens/s per GPU. INT8 tuned gave us median p99 85ms and throughput up to 360 tokens/s with continuous batching. Cost per token estimated down ~2.8x on your traffic mix. FP8 tests were somewhere between both — about 1.8x cost reduction with much closer quality to FP16 on classification workloads.
[03:10] Maya: wait you said 360 tokens per second with INT8? that seems high versus what we've seen. are those synthetic workloads?
[03:20] Samir: good call — it's a mixed workload bench with real prompt distribution you provided, includes many short chat turns which batch well. our synthetic small-batch runs hit lower numbers. there is variance tied to sequence length.
[04:05] David: how about memory/KV cache? we saw evictions in our first run.
[04:12] Samir: KV caching behavior is different with quantized models — the footprint is smaller but alignment of offsets can cause slightly different cache eviction patterns, sometimes more frequent for many concurrent long contexts. for canary we recommend pinning prefix cache and monitoring the cache hit ratio.
[05:00] Maya: quality — where are we seeing regressions?
[05:05] Samir: two main buckets. one: NER and short extraction templates — precision drop by ~3-5% in INT8 versus FP16 on your labeled set. two: a date-parsing prompt where INT8 introduced formatting inconsistencies — more abbreviations and occasionally wrong timezone offsets. FP8 reduced both effects to near-baseline.
[05:50] Jordan: can you replay an example?
[06:00] Samir: sure -- sample prompt: "extract appointment date from message" FP16 -> "June 12, 2026 09:00 PDT" INT8 -> "Jun 12th 09:00" or occasionally "June 12 6am" which is off due to timezone misinterpretation.
[06:35] Maya: hum that could break our downstream schedulers.
[06:40] Lena: yep and that's why we want a canary with strict assertion checks.

[07:10] Tomas: curious if this is a numeric stability issue with certain attention kernels? our theory: the relative scaling in quantization changes the softmax tail behavior.
[07:25] Samir: totally possible — we observed slight attention weight sharpening on a subset of samples, which amplifies or mutes small signals.
[07:40] Samir: also worth noting our current quant pipeline uses symmetric per-tensor scales for speed. switching to per-channel scales reduces some regressions but increases compute slightly; FP8 already uses per-channel by default in our build.

[08:30] Priya: network / infra question — if we do a private? Does Redwood support KMS rotation and can we do HSM-backed keys?
[08:40] Lena: yes on Redwood Private we integrate with customer KMS and HSM is supported in the on-prem bundle; rotation windows are configurable. we'll share the security brief.

[09:05] Evan: what about fallback logic — if INT8 sway beyond threshold do we fall back to FP16 or to FP8?
[09:15] Samir: recommended fallback order: first try FP8 variant (lowest perf hit, often restores quality), if still failing then FP16. the routing can be policy-driven per route and thresholded by live evals.
[10:00] Maya: how do we detect failure in-flight? we'd rather not do human review every time.
[10:08] Samir: you can instrument per-prompt assertions: regex/date checks, NER label count sanity checks; additionally we have a small L0 eval that runs on a sampling stream (1% by default) with micro-evals that return a pass/fail score to the router. If fail rate passes threshold autopromote fallback or pause rollout.

[11:10] Jordan: what impact does batching have on latency SLO? some of our user journeys need sub-200ms end-to-end.
[11:20] Samir: batching helps throughput but inflates tail latency when batch windows wait. we can enforce max batching latency (e.g., 10ms) and per-route SLO overrides. for short-turn flows we recommend smaller batch sizes and KV prewarm.

[12:50] Samir: moving to the signal analysis — we created a heatmap across prompt templates showing delta in F1 and token-latency tradeoff for INT8 and FP8. show slide... (link in chat). we flagged 7 templates with >2% F1 drop in INT8; FP8 reduced that to <0.7% for 5 of those. two templates remain problematic.

[14:30] Maya: which templates exactly? are they long-context retrieval style or short QA?
[14:40] Samir: short QA with time expressions and enumerations — they rely on subtle punctuation and tokenization quirks. also one template uses date locales which interacts badly with quant rounding in logits.

[15:20] Lena: note we may be seeing tokenizer boundary effects — sometimes quant noise pushes tokens to an adjacent token causing off-by-one tokenization. we can try re-tokenizing those templates or small prompt rephrasing as a mitigation.

[16:00] Tomas: have you tried calibration with a small high-precision float pass for the head tokens? like do first 2 tokens FP16 then the rest quantized?
[16:12] Samir: we've tested hybrid prefix heuristics — running the first N layers in FP16 or keeping first T tokens in high precision reduces initial misfires. it adds a small cost but is effective for short-answer templates. we can include that as an experimental knob in the canary.

[17:10] David: cost modeling — can you break down expected delta for our traffic mix if we do an FP8 canary for 10% traffic then roll to INT8?
[17:25] Samir: rough estimate: FP8 at 10% reduces overall cost by ~8% while keeping quality near baseline, INT8 full rollout could hit ~20-25% reduction but with the observed risk areas. so a staged move FP8 -> INT8 with targeted holdouts is lower risk.

[18:45] Maya: SLA concern: our legal wants to see rollback within 1 hour if any regression hits production. can Redwood automate that?
[18:55] Iris: yes — Redwood Console can trigger automatic route-level rollback based on micro-eval thresholds and has a playbook webhook to notify your incident system. we can show a demo during the canary run.

[19:30] Jordan: test coverage — we need a reproducible testcase for the two failing templates, please capture seeds.
[19:38] Samir: agreed, please share the failing inputs from your end, we will also sample failing traces and build minimal repros.

[20:20] Samir: quick demo — looking at a live trace where INT8 fails: you can see the attention map shifts and token logit softening around punctuation which causes the date to lose AM/PM. FP8 restores the sharpness.

[22:00] Maya: can you add a TTL on KV cache entries to avoid stale prefix collisions during canary?
[22:06] Samir: yes TTL is configurable per-deployment; we suggest short TTLs during canary to avoid sticky artifacts, then increase after stable.

[23:10] Toms (note: speaker tag glitched as "Tom's"): yeah also watch for training-set leakage in the eval set -- we had an example where a templated answer looks right but is memorized.

[24:00] Samir: good call; our micro-eval will check novelty heuristics and n-gram overlap to detect memorized outputs.

[25:20] Lena: can we capture the proposed canary timeline? i think customer suggested a two week phased pilot?
[25:28] Maya: yes two weeks with first 3 days smoke, next week FP8 rollout to 10-20% with micro-evals, then week two expand or pivot to INT8 for non-sensitive routes.

[26:00] Samir: recommended checklist items for canary: 1) build repro tests for flagged templates, 2) configure micro-eval stream and thresholds, 3) set KV cache TTL and prefix pinning, 4) prepare FP8 fallback and FP16 final fallback policies, 5) monitor SNR and set auto-rollback at 1.5% absolute F1 drop or RTT spikes above threshold.

[27:15] Priya: monitoring integration — can we push metrics to our prometheus?
[27:20] Iris: yes, Redwood supports Prometheus exporters for token/time metrics and has alerting hooks to PagerDuty/Slack.

[28:10] Maya: performance variance — we saw a single node that spiked p99 to 420ms intermittently. is that GPU jitter or memory garbage?
[28:20] Samir: looks like host-level interference in that run; we recommend isolating noise by using dedicated pinned capacity for the canary (Redwood Dedicated) or strict node affinity in your private deployment.

[29:05] David: curious about telemetry retention for security — how long are traces kept?
[29:12] Lena: default is 30 days but we can extend retention or disable transcript capture; in Private you control retention and PII redaction. security deck in chat covers SOC2 details.

[30:00] Evan: any blockers on our side before canary?
[30:06] Maya: need to finalize the eval set and confirm which routes are sensitive (schedulers, payment flows).

[30:22] Lena: we'll send a template for route classification and an example eval set format.

[31:15] Samir: technical note — when we roll INT8 we should run a nightly calibration job for the temperature/scaling factors; it reduces drift across versions.

[31:50] Jordan: also, add QA acceptance criteria to the canary plan: acceptance = micro-eval pass rate >= 99% of baseline and no increase in high-priority incidents.

[32:20] Lena: recap of key decisions: 1) proceed with FP8 pilot to 10% first, 2) run 5k sensitivity sweep concurrently, 3) prepare repro cases for 2 problematic templates, 4) configure micro-eval + auto-rollback, 5) use shorter KV TTL and consider prefix pin for canary.

[33:10] Maya: timeline: expecting results from Samir by 08/19, pricing from Lena by 08/14, and canary kickoff targeted 08/24.

[34:00] Samir: ok I'll start the sensitivity sweep job after the call; I'll also push a flagged-set CSV into the benchmark sheet with per-sample deltas.

[35:10] Lena: anything else?
[35:20] Priya: one ask — can we have a dry-run of the rollback automation into our staging incident flow?
[35:28] Iris: yes we'll schedule a 30 minute dry-run with your SREs.

[36:00] Lena: thanks everyone. we'll send notes and update the pilot doc. expect the pricing + canary playbook by Friday.
[36:12] Maya: thanks all.
[36:15] David: thanks.
[36:18] Tomas: thanks.
[36:20] Lena: end.

End of transcript.
